text:
maria_sre: FYI — we're seeing allocation failures and high attach latency in eu-central1 GPU pools. Control-plane heartbeats show inter-zone packet loss and the upstream provider has an ongoing reroute. Provisioning is timing out on driver registration.

ops_bot: ALERT: eu-central1-gpu: 95th latency > 1200ms, allocation failure rate 18% (5m window)

kyle_infra: Can you paste the driver logs? trying to correlate with kernel oops or nvlink errors.

maria_sre: here's the common stack we see on attach:
```
2025-11-03T09:12:44Z attach: driver_register timeout
err: NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED
retry 3/3 -> provisioning failed
```

nina_prod: Looks like the fabric path between eu-central1-a and -b is flapping at the TOR layer; control plane retries are amplifying. We should consider partial traffic steering to eu-west1 while infra teams confirm.

julia_support: We have several active enterprise escalations (Acme, FinData). Need an approved customer-facing blurb ASAP — they want ETA and if their jobs will be prioritized.

matt_oncall: Action plan: 
1) Start graceful drift -> drain affected racks (eu-central1-a,b) for workload reconvergence.
2) Apply routing policy to shift new allocations to eu-west1 with enterprise priority preserved.
3) Temporarily lower concurrency for non-enterprise tenants (throttle token rate).
ETA for initial mitigation: 45m.

kyle_infra: Commands I'm about to run:
```bash
# limit new allocations from eu-central1
redwoodctl route update --from eu-central1 --to eu-west1 --weight 40
# prioritize enterprise tenants
redwoodctl route update --priority enterprise --preserve
# drain hosts to trigger graceful eviction
kubectl cordon r-gpu-ec1-0{12..15}
kubectl drain r-gpu-ec1-012 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
```

kyle_infra: Note — shifting to eu-west1 will increase per-token cost ~28% for on-demand capacity; should we accept for customer SLAs?

aaron_sales: Prioritize enterprise tenants (Acme, FinData). If we have to absorb cost spikes for 1-2 hours to preserve SLA, sales is ok; we need a short notice to customers with expected ETA and whether there will be degraded throughput.

nina_prod: Agree on prioritization. I'll set a traffic policy: enterprise weight -> 80% to stable pools, standard -> throttled to 50% of baseline while we stabilize.

julia_support: Draft status page message for review: "We are investigating elevated allocation failures and latency in eu-central1 affecting GPU provisioning. We are routing new workloads to eu-west1 and prioritizing enterprise customers. Estimated mitigation in 45 minutes. Customers with escalations will receive updates via direct support channels. — Redwood Ops" Any changes?

maria_sre: Add note about potential cost-based fallbacks: "We may provision short-lived on-demand capacity to meet SLAs; this may affect cost but not customer billing tiers."

julia_support: Updated status: "We are investigating elevated GPU provisioning failures in eu-central1 caused by upstream interconnect instability. We are shifting new allocations to eu-west1 and prioritizing enterprise customers; mitigation estimate 45 minutes. Impact: delayed job starts and higher latency for non-priority workloads. Enterprise customers with active escalations are being contacted directly." Posting now?

matt_oncall: Post initial status page update and pin this thread. I'll start the routing commands now. Please monitor allocation logs and paste any regression.

nina_prod: Routing change applied: 40% -> eu-west1, enterprise preserved. Watching per-host attach success rates.

kyle_infra: Drain started on r-gpu-ec1-012..015. Evictions happening; preemptible jobs being requeued.

maria_sre: Attach success rate improved from 82% -> 95% for shifted requests within 12 minutes of routing change. Still seeing control-plane retransmits for old sessions.

julia_support: Sent direct messages to Acme & FinData CSMs with ETA and mitigation steps. Sales updated.

aaron_sales: Thx — please flag if we need to route any high-value long-running jobs to dedicated pools (we can authorize temporary dedicated capacity).

matt_oncall: OK — if attach rates stay >93% for 15m we'll mark incident as mitigation achieved and move to monitoring. If not, we escalate to provider for circuit remediation and consider multi-region forced failover.

ops_bot: UPDATE: mitigation in progress, 95th attach latency -> 480ms, allocation failure -> 6%

maria_sre: Good work. I'll keep this thread open and post final RCA timeline. For now: status page up, customers notified, enterprise prioritized, cost tradeoffs accepted for short window.

julia_support: I'll prepare a follow-up customer note in 2 hours with more detail and next steps.

matt_oncall: Closing action: keep monitoring until 10:30 UTC, then reconvene for RCA prep. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
